ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle ACD = \angle BCE = 90^\circ$. If $\angle ACB = 150^\circ$, can you calculate the measure of $\angle DCE$? Please write down the solution process.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ACD = \angle BCE = 90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD + \angle ECB = 180^\circ$\\
Also, since $\angle ACB + \angle ECD = \angle ACD + \angle ECB = 180^\circ$, and $\angle ACB = 150^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ECD = 180^\circ - \angle ACB = \boxed{30^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, point C is below, A is at the lower left, B is on the right, D is above, and E is at the upper left. Starting from point C, inside ∠ACB, the order of the rays that can be seen is CA, CE, CD, CB. Therefore ∠ACB is divided into three adjacent angles: ∠ACE, ∠ECD, ∠DCB, among which the required ∠DCE is ∠ECD. Then reason: Let ∠DCE = ∠ECD = x. Because the problem gives ∠ACD = 90°, and ∠ACD = ∠ACE + ∠ECD, so ∠ACE + x = 90°, that is, ∠ACE = 90° - x. Also because ∠BCE = 90°, and ∠BCE = ∠BCD + ∠DCE, so ∠DCB + x = 90°, that is, ∠DCB = 90° - x. Thus ∠ACB = ∠ACE + ∠ECD + ∠DCB = (90° - x) + x + (90° - x) = 180° - x. It is known that ∠ACB = 150°, so 150° = 180° - x, solving gives x = 30°. Therefore ∠DCE = 30°.
